items.name: FoSho
items.summary: The product I am currently working on at Metra.
items.detail: Working on FoSho has been as much about product judgement and team trust as implementation: decide what actually matters, give people room to do good work, and keep the experience simple.

items.name: SteamPriceChecker
items.summary: Compare Steam game prices across regions and push price notifications through Discord.
items.detail: A practical automation tool built around a very simple question: can checking regional pricing be less annoying?

items.name: ToneTrace
items.summary: Identify the likely guitar amp and effect chain behind a tone, whether it comes from a recording or something playing live.
items.detail: The interface should stay stupidly simple even if the signal analysis underneath becomes complicated: listen, analyse, explain the likely chain.

items.name: ReHandShaker 2.0
items.summary: A cleaner second pass at Android ↔ macOS file transfer, with the Mac side treated as a real native app instead of a wrapper.
items.detail: The goal is not “more features”. It is making a common cross-device task feel obvious: native macOS UI, minimal setup and as little friction as possible.

items.name: No One Was Here
items.summary: A game idea about memory, the past and the uncomfortable question of whether changing cages counts as freedom.
items.detail: Are you really free, or did you just hop into a new cage? It stays here as an idea until there is something real to build.

about.name: Ivan Chan
about.bio: I don't care much whether something sounds technically impressive. I care whether it turns an annoying task into an obvious one.

inspirations.eyebrow: things I keep coming back to
inspirations.title: Inspirations
inspirations.intro: Not a canon. Just people and work that left fingerprints on how I see things.

directors.title: Directors
directors.description: Framing, silence, rhythm and the courage to let a scene be strange.

items.label: Jiang Wen
items.note: Satire, cultural layering and the ability to make chaos feel completely deliberate.

items.label: Quentin Tarantino
items.note: Dialogue as violence; rhythm as narrative.

items.label: Stanley Kubrick
items.note: Precision, geometry and dread — every frame feels loaded.

games.title: Games
games.description: Games that made atmosphere, systems or memory feel more important than spectacle.

items.label: Life Is Strange
items.note: Choices, mood and music — one of those games where everything emotionally clicks.

items.label: P.T
items.note: The scariest hallway ever made. Minimal space, maximum pressure.

items.label: Metal Gear
items.note: Story colliding with systems, politics and wonderfully unnecessary ideas.

items.label: Cyberpunk 2077
items.note: The city as a character; neon future as melancholy.

music.title: Music
music.description: The records and artists that keep leaking into how I think about texture, space and emotion.

items.label: Tame Impala
items.note: Psychedelic texture, bass lines and distortion that still knows how to groove.

items.label: JPEGMAFIA
items.note: Noise, glitches and ugly sounds arranged with ridiculous intention.

items.label: Mk.gee
items.note: Warped guitars, negative space and songs that feel half-broken but completely alive.

items.label: Porter Robinson
items.note: Electronic music with sincerity at its core. Nurture made vulnerability feel enormous.

items.label: Flume
items.note: Digital artefacts turned into musical texture.

items.label: Jack White
items.note: Raw electricity, compression and fuzz without sanding off the edges.

items.label: Radiohead
items.note: Anxiety, atmosphere and arrangement as architecture.
